newsitem.title: USA: Eighth soldier charged in Aberdeen sex probe.
newsitem.headline: Eighth soldier charged in Aberdeen sex probe.

text.p: An eighth soldier at the Army's Aberdeen Proving Ground has been charged with sexual misconduct, Army officials said Wednesday.

The Army said Staff Sgt. Herman Gunter, 30, was formally charged Monday with two instances of rape as well as sexual harassment, assault, adultery and obstruction of justice in cases involving a total of three trainees at the proving ground's Ordnance Centre and School.
Gunter was the fourth soldier at the base charged with rape in connection with the probe. Four others have been charged with lesser offences.
Two of those charged have elected to receive discharges in lieu of court-martial, and the Army agreed to hear one other case at a non-judicial punishment hearing.

The announcement of Gunter's charges followed statements by five women soldiers from the proving ground Tuesday that military investigators had pressured them to falsely say they were raped by superiors at the base.

The women said at a news conference Tuesday one of the soldiers the women had been involved with was charged Tuesday in a case not involving them, but Army officals were not immediately able to confirm whether Gunter was the soldier to which the women were referring.
